name: The Man in the Moon

attacks.name: :O
attacks.description: A breath attack that fans out in a wide radius from the head, dealing 10 knockback to units caught in the blast. This attack is prepared at the start of every round, and cast at the end of the round. * This attack does not deal knockback to the hands.

attacks.name: Call for Help
attacks.description: Spawns 4 B-Probers on random tiles. This attack can only be used once per fight, and only after The Man in the Moon's health reaches below 25%.

wikiBehavior:
The Man in the Moon consists of three parts - a stationary head, and two hands that move and attack independently. The head starts with [[status:Brace]], and the hands will only take 1 damage per attack.

The Moon Hands move toward units and use a melee attack. If a unit ends its movement *in front of* the palm of the hand, it will grab the unit, disabling all actions and replacing their basic attack with Flail, which deals damage and has a 25% chance to release the unit. Attacking the hand from behind will force it to release the captive unit. The hand can be attacked from any direction to turn it away from the unit that attacked it. If attacked from behind while not holding a unit, it will charge forward, trampling anything in its path. If it collides with the head, it deals 20 damage and removes its Brace until its next turn. This can be repeated to deal further damage.

The head will immediately prepare a wide breath attack on its first turn. If a cat or other allied unit ends it movement in the tile directly in front of its mouth, the unit will be eaten, replacing their actions with two choices: Flail,  and Stop Hitting Yourself, a spell that commands the Moon Hands to charge toward the head. On the head's second turn, it will cast its breath attack - or, if it has eaten a cat, it will munch on it and deal damage. If the unit is a familiar, it will be swallowed.
wikiStrategies:
* The player should bait the hands towards the three center columns of the map, then turn the hands towards the face and make them dash as to break the [[status:Brace]]. Any further face dash on this turn will deal 20 damage to the boss. This makes having a higher quantity of attacks more important than those attacks dealing much damage, as the hands ram into the Man in the Moon multiple times per turn. 
** Note that multi-attacks, such as [[ability:Fury Swipes]], will only ram into the boss once.
** Attacks that have no damage or knockback will still cause the hands to attack, for example, using [[ability:Lick]] on a hand will make it dash.
** This means that the player needs to be mindful about accidentally inflicting status effects such as [[status:Stun]] on the hands as they will not be able to ram into the boss.
* Ending movement in front of the Man in the Moon while his mouth is open will make him swallow the cat. On that cat's turn, it can flail to escape, but additionally can cast a 10 mana spell called "Stop Hitting Yourself", which will force the two hands to dash attack it. This is a guaranteed way to remove the brace buff.
** This causes contact damage to the cat, as Man in the Moon will chew it. Letting him swallow a cat with high constitution and contact effects such as [[status:Thorns]] allows it to deal more damage as well as taking the hits. The [[class:Butcher]] and [[class:Necromancer]] classes can potentially have high-enough Mana and Health to consistently make it work, while the [[class:Tank]] class can manage the Thorns.
** If a cat is downed while inside Man in the Moon, they will be instantly killed and swallowed by Man in the Moon.
** A cat will only be initially swallowed if it ends its movement in the middle of the Man in the Moon's front 3 tiles.
** If a cat is inside the Man in the Moon when the boss dies, it will survive.
* The Hands die when the Man in the Moon dies.
** The Hands are also immune to all status effects, meaning [[status:Thorns]] cannot be applied to increase their damage to the Man in the Moon.
* The Man in the Moon will only charge his ":O" attack when it's his first turn in the round. If his attack is interrupted, he won't attack and will only charge it next turn. The player can interrupt his attack by getting him to eat a unit.
* If a cat has the [[item:Frying Pan]] equipped, it can ignore almost all damage and focus on the boss by having one side exposed.
* If an Amoeba is brought to the fight and takes the Man in the Moon, destroying it with [[ability:Reap]] will instantly kill the boss.
** Players should be careful when bringing Amoeba to the fight, as if they don't have [[ability:Reap]] or similar abilities, it can prolong the fight.
*** An Amoeba that has taken the Man in the Moon as a shield can still be captured by the hands, which can make it even more difficult to end the fight if the player is not prepared.
* Due to the nature of the fight, any AI controlled allied units like Mini-Me's can be extremely detrimental, as they mess up the hands and activate their counter attacks.
** For this reason, the Severe Deja Vu punishment inflicted by NPC should be avoided at all costs, even if the player has strong cats.
* Inflicting [[status:Stun]] on the Man in the Moon while its [[status:Brace]] is depleted will prevent it from regenerating the Brace on the next turn.
*using [[item:Weird Egg]] to spawn a Brain Drain and having it use Counterspell will cancel Man in the Moon from regenerating his [[status:Brace]].
*[[ability:Bloodletting]], [[ability:Reset]] and [[ability:Hack]] can remove Man in the Moon's [[status:Brace]] without cracking it so it won't regenerate the [[status:Brace]].
*Inflicting [[status:Bruise]] will offset Man in the Moon's [[status:Brace]].
wikiNotes:

wikiQuotes: They will crawl on their bellies and eat dust!

wikiTrivia:

name: The Mother
wikiBehavior:
* Every turn, The Mother will  expand across the arena by spawning 5 HP tumor segments.
* These segments propagate semi-randomly, one space at a time, to any adjacent space that is not already occupied by an existing segment. If left alive, they will grow, and heal to 9 [[stat:HEALTH]] at the end of the round.
** If a segment is not attached to The Mother after its neighboring segment is destroyed, it will automatically get destroyed.
* If a unit is on a tile that a segment appears on, that unit is captured, and their basic attack will be reduced with [[ability:Struggle]], disabling all their abilities until freed.
** The segment can be destroyed to free them, unharmed.
** If a big tumor is holding a unit, it will consume them at the end of the round.
* The Mother's basic attack spawns a pillar underneath the farthest allied unit, dealing 3 damage and hurling them 2 tiles towards the main body. Each pillar has [[status:Thorns]].
* At 25% health (122), The Mother will turn all pillars into Heralds.

*The Mother takes 2 turns per round.

*The Mother and all of her segments are knockback immune.
** The segments are do not take extra damage from backstabs, cannot be stunned and won't leave a corpse.
wikiStrategies:
* Attacks that can hit multiple targets should be prioritized to destroy multiple sections and stop the tumors from growing and spreading.
** [[ability:Scatter Shot]] being an especially potent example, able to hit each tile individually.
* It is advised to keep a unit that can deal at least 5 ranged damage away from the main body to quickly free allies if they are caught, as well as deal with the spikes.
** If the player lacks ranged units, multiple allied summons may accomplish the same goal.
* Being a 3x3 sized unit, Mother is highly vulnerable to debuffs that automatically get applied to every tile at the start of battle Such as [[item:Leech Brood]], which will apply 9 stacks of [[status:Leeches]].
* Ability and weapon focused builds are recommended, as [[ability:Struggle]] will replace captured units' basic.
* Stacking [[status:Thorns]] and other on-contact damage effects can be useful tow instantly destroy the tumors when captured.
** This only applies to units with at least 5 retaliatory damage.
* Items and Abilities that trigger on kill (such as [[item:Red Cap]] and [[ability:Luck Drain]]) are very strong in this fight, since each segment of The Mother is a separate unit.
** Additionally, a cat that can deal at least 9 damage and has Blood Frenzy can easily clear most of her segments.
** [[ability:OVERPOWERED!!!]] can start a chain reaction of explosions with segments next to Mother, damaging her.
* [[item:The Tick]] can aid greatly in this fight, as all segments Mother spawns will also have [[status:All Stats Down]], reducing their health.
* A ranged attacker with [[ability:Sentry Mode]] or [[ability:Tower Defense]] can kill new segments as they spawn.
* The [[item:Weird Egg]] can summon Brain Drain familiars which can be highly beneficial to this fight, as their [[ability:Counterspell]] will prevent The Mother from growing her tumors and prevent their instakill effect.

wikiNotes:
* The Mother's rare, unique boss drops are: [[item:Mother's Teeth]] & [[item:Mother's Love]].
* Cannot gain [[status:Elite Buff: Twin]].
* The hole in the ground left after The Mother's death is not an object; it is her corpse, and as such, can be interacted with like with any other corpse.
wikiQuotes: Look what has become of me...
My children have returned to me!
wikiTrivia:
* The Mother is based on an enemy from [[url:https://theendisnigh.fandom.com/wiki/Mother|The End is Nigh]], who was described by Edmund Mcmillen as "mother nature" and "the bringer and taker of life".
* The Mother bears some resemblance to The Beast, the final boss of The Binding of Isaac: Repentance, mainly in her intro card.
** This is even more apparent with her Champion form, where she sports red eyes similar to The Beast.
** Additionally, the [[item:Mother's Love]] item drop features the same polka-dot pattern present on the dress of both The Beast and Mom.
** The Mother's unique boss drops both give three stat bonuses with values of six; the number 666 (three sixes) is described as "the number of the Beast" in the Bible.
* The Mother also bears some resemblance to the Tormentor.
** The Mother’s spawns closely resemble the tumor-themed enemies of [[chapter:The Core]].
*** Other enemies in this chapter also resemble enemies from The Core, such as Slag resembling Mega Tumor, furthering the connection.

*If the Throbbing King's corpse is looted with 1 cat in the party then there will be a stem cat in the success cutscene where the rest of the party usually is.

* The Throbbing King's song calls him a "monarchy", rather than a monarch, implying that the Throbbing Domain might be an extension of him.

name: Zaratana
wikiBehavior: Similarly to Pyrophina, despite her massive size, Zaratana takes up only 4 tiles, often attempting to walk all over the party with Trample before performing an attack. She is able to crowd the map quickly with rocks, grant them levitation effects, and summon a debilitating Meteornado at half health.
wikiStrategies:
* [[ability:Eat Rock]] can be used in combat to great effect. Zaratana herself is considered a rock by the ability and can be attacked by it for 5 damage alongside the auxiliary effects.
* [[ability:Butcher]] will instantly destroy all of Zaratana’s rocks in a single turn.
wikiTrivia:
* Much like how Pyrophina is likely a pastiche of Godzilla, Zaratana is likely one of Gamera, a turtle-like Kaiju often considered one of the most influential Kaiju franchises in Japan alongside Godzilla.
** Zaratana may also draw inspiration from legendary Pokémon, Pyrophina and Zaratana both represent opposite concepts (far below at the centre of the earth vs high above in space) and can passively generate weather conditions similar to legendary Pokémon such as Groudon and Kyogre. The player can additionally select one of the two to join them on their adventure.
* Zaratana's Intro plays a rendition of Also Sprach Zarathustra's fanfare "Sunrise" well known for its use in 2001: A Space Odyssey.
**Zaratana's name derives from the song's title "Zara" while retaining the naming convention of Act 1 and 2 House Bosses ending in "na"

name: Zodiac
wikiBehavior: Zodiac shoots in the direction of anything that moves to another tile, including objects that have been moved. He does not shoot cats that perform actions which do not move them to another tile. Zodiac has six shots in his revolver. Trying to fire a seventh shot will result in him attempting to shoot before getting confused and putting his gun away. During Zodiac's turn, he moves to a random tile, and may fire a shot if he has any bullets left. If he runs out of bullets before or during the turn, he will also reload his gun.
wikiStrategies:
* Hiding behind cover and moving the various objects around the map to bait out Zodiac's shots can provide a window of opportunity to attack.
* Spawning familiars or using [[ability:Dump]] can be used as another method to bait out Zodiac's shots.
* Classes with ranged basic attacks (e.g. [[class:Hunter]] & [[class:Mage]]) are great as they can attack from afar without having to move, often countering his main gimmick.
* Classes with high constitution (e.g. [[class:Tank]] & [[class:Cleric]]) can absorb more shots from Zodiac, allowing them to approach and attack him without relying as much on cover.
* Stacking armor effects can mitigate the damage from one or two shots, opening up opportunities to attack.
* Zodiac only reloads if he is out of bullets during his turn. This can be taken advantage of by leaving Zodiac on low ammo so he doesn’t reload, allowing quick depletion of his remaining ammo during the round.
wikiNotes:
* Zodiac's rare, unique boss drops are: [[item:Zodiacs Poncho]] & [[item:Zodiac's Six Shooter]].

wikiTrivia:
* The insignia on Zodiac's cloak is the stamp used by the unidentified serial killer known as the "[[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer|Zodiac Killer]]", who is also one of his inspirations and his namesake.
** The quote "I want to report a murder... no, a double murder." is likely inspired by a quote from the Zodiac Killer.
* npc, Guillotina and Zodiac were of the second set of characters to recieve plushies as merchandise for the game, following Stacy and Radical Rat.

* Zodiac used to be a mini-boss. Zodiac's conception and development was heavily documented in the [[url:https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/686060?emclan=103582791472650338&emgid=4213757668856197864|"Zodiac!"]] blog post.
** Zodiac was conceived due to the developers wanting a cat mini-boss in the game who used a gun and from needing a mini-boss for The Desert. He was first prototyped as a enemy using the regular cat pieces who fired his revolver once any of his enemies ended their turns and during this time, he was known as simply "Gunslinger" by Tyler Glaiel. After deciding it wasn't fun, he experimented with instead having him fire the gun whenever he detected movement. There wouldn't be any more mechanical changes to Zodiac after this, as the change of having him react to movement was decided to be fun enough to not warrant another change. As for Zodiac's design, he was made bipedal due to Edmund McMillen wanting to make Zodiac stand out due to the fact he was going to be a mini-boss. Edmund McMillen cited him as a combination of "[[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirty_Harry_(character)|Dirty Harry]] and the Zodiac Killer". When the developers began playtesting sessions with The Desert, it was noticed that Zodiac overshadowed the already existing boss of the chapter in terms of character and design. With this, it was decided to elevate Zodiac from a mini-boss to a full-fledged boss of the chapter.
